modifier.description:
Value type modifier

Non empty constraint is specified by adding an exclamation mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  where: !Location
```

The desire to preserve empty values (such that they can be differentiated from the lack of any value) is specified
by adding a question mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  approved: ?boolean
```

The non optional function parameter constraint is specified by adding `!?` in front of the ValueType:
```type
  f: function(url: !?string serialized Url)
```

@see #isNonEmpty
@see #preservesEmpty
@see #isNonOptionalParam
@see FunctionParam#isNonOptional

keyType.description:
The value type for the keys that index the collection.
For array and set, the key is `int` and for stream is the key is not used.
For maps, the key can be any primitive type.

elementType.description: The value type for the elements of the collection.

size.description: The declared size of the vector.

title:
A vector is a fixed-size array of `float`s. This is used for large arrays of numeric values.

Vectors are declared in DSL using brackets containing the _size_:
```type
samples: [10_000]
```

Note that this syntax is similar to the {@link ArrayType array} syntax, but distinct because a literal integer value
replaces the element type between the brackets. Vectors are also arrays so all the array operations work on them.
The instance type is {@link Vector}, which extends **Array**.

Unlike other collection types, vectors will _not_ have a default empty value, so will either be null or have the
full set of values. Note that the #size must be positive, so there are no non-null empty vectors.

@see Vector
@see ArrayType
name: VectorType
